text:
Palworld 1.0: Easy Ore and Ingot Farming Guide
If you’re just starting your journey in Palworld, you have likely realized that ore is a heavy, difficult resource to find and continuously harvest. Until you reach Level 24 and unlock your very own Ore Mining Site, scrambling for enough materials can bring your progression to a crawl. Fortunately, there are a couple of methods you can exercise to speed up your progress and save yourself a massive headache.

By setting up a second base behind the Desolate Church, you can establish a substantial and self-sufficient ore farm. Utilizing Pals like Rushoar for their charge attacks, or Digtoise to grind deposits into dust, will dramatically increase your mining efficiency. Combined with version 1.0's new Easy Bulk Storage feature to manage your weight limit, as well as Foxsparks and Lamballs to automate the smelting and transport, you will secure a steady stream of ore and ingots to power your playthrough.

author: IGN YouTube
text:
Palworld 1.0 - Best Ways to Get Hardwood Quickly!
Palworld 1.0 introduces dense new milestones for your survival progression, and grabbing a ton of Hardwood is an essential step for the midgame. If you're struggling to spot these specific trees in the wild or just want to figure out the best ways to keep your base's stockpiles full, here is everything you need to know to get chopping.

Finding Hardwood in Palworld requires venturing into higher-level areas like the Twilight Dunes and knowing exactly which trees to hit. Once you locate this valuable lumber, farming Hardwood efficiently means utilizing fast-travel points, setting up satellite bases with Lumbering Pals, and eventually unlocking the Logging Site II facility at level 43. By combining these methods, you can create an infinitely renewable source of materials so you can focus on other challenges across the map.

text:
Plans for Fallout, Elder Scrolls, More Revealed in Bethesda Studios Roadmap - IGN Daily Fix
In today's Daily Fix:
It's been almost nothing but bad news for Xbox and its subsidiaries ever since CEO Asha Sharma announced the great and terrible Xbox reset of 2026. But there is some silver lining to all of the chaos: Bethesda Studios head Todd Howard has announced a roadmap for the company's IP including Fallout, The Elder Scrolls, and Starfield. Confirmed are remakes of Fallout 3 and New Vegas, and the next mainline game, Fallout 5, is in development. But right now their biggest priority is The Elder Scrolls 6, which we've seen nothing of save for a teaser trailer back in 2018. In other gaming adjacent news, the God of War live-action series encountered a major setback when star Ryan Hurst suffered a torn bicep and will need to be recast. Apparently the recovery time will be too long and his 12-year-old co-star Callum Vinson will likely have aged noticeably enough for the footage not to match. And finally, we have this week's latest gaming releases.
